business_model: Subscription SaaS plus payment-processing take-rate, merchant-count-driven

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2006 in Ottawa, Canada by Tobias Lütke, Daniel Weinand, and Scott Lake, providing e-commerce storefront software allowing merchants to build and run online stores.
historical_evidence.market: Large and growing SMB e-commerce infrastructure market, with the company by this point also expanding into offline/point-of-sale retail, broadening its addressable market beyond pure online storefronts.
historical_evidence.team: Founding team had operated the company for roughly seven years by the snapshot date, having scaled it through multiple funding rounds and a substantial, disclosed merchant-growth trajectory.
historical_evidence.product: E-commerce platform enabling merchants to build online stores, recently expanded to support offline/point-of-sale retail as well, positioning the company as a broader 'commerce' platform rather than a purely online storefront tool.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $100M in Series C funding in December 2013, led by OMERS Ventures and Insight Venture Partners (with Bessemer Venture Partners, FirstMark Capital, and others participating), at a valuation reported as 'near $1 billion.'
historical_evidence.traction: Disclosed merchant count grew from approximately 20,000 stores in 2010 to over 80,000 by the snapshot date — a real, specific, disclosed four-year growth trajectory. Merchants had also sold well over $1.5 billion in cumulative product volume through the platform by the end of 2013.
historical_evidence.financial: No specific company revenue figures (as distinct from merchant gross-merchandise-volume) were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for the December 2013 snapshot.

sources.title: Shopify Raises $100M To Drop The 'E' And Become The Commerce Company That Spans On- And Offline
